text: It is not produced. This is said to be the mere reference to the sign (linga). Therefore, the knowledge that “the mountain is fiery” arises through inference. This is self-directed inference (svārtha-anumāna). However, when one infers fire from smoke for oneself and then employs a five-membered syllogism to convey this understanding to another, that is other-directed inference (parārtha-anumāna). For example: “The mountain is fiery because it has smoke. Whatever has smoke has fire, as is the case with a large kitchen. This mountain is likewise. Therefore, it is so.” By this, another person comes to understand the fire through the sign (linga) established by this argument. || 41 ||
